name: [R24] Application worker crash near Brotli context, consistent with CVE-2026-111497 ("Node2Shell"/"HTTP2Shell") -- exploratory heuristic, no published IOC
message:
Indicators of CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can leak memory or lead to RCE when decompressing attacker-controlled Brotli data. Originally disclosed against Node.js ("Node2Shell", fixed 2026-10-21 in 22.23.4/24.22.1/26.12.1), then found to affect PyPI packages `brotli` (1.0.3-1.2.0, fixed 1.2.1) and `brotlicffi` (1.0.3-1.2.0.x, fixed 1.2.1.0) via GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35 (critical, 2026-10-22). requests/httpx/aiohttp auto-load these packages when present, so exposure is broader than direct `import brotli` use. Aikido's unverified claim (2026-10-23) extends this to "HTTP2Shell" -- any HTTP client/server decompressing Brotli.

NO VENDOR OR RESEARCHER HAS PUBLISHED A REQUEST-LEVEL OR LOG-LEVEL IOC for this CVE (unlike wp2shell/R13 or PHP2Shell/R15) -- this is this repo's own constructed heuristic, not a confirmed signature: a generic WSGI/application worker crash (gunicorn/uwsgi patterns) near "brotli" context. Weak, unconfirmed signal -- treat a hit as a lead, not evidence. Confirm the installed brotli/brotlicffi version with scripts/python_brotli_check.py; as of 2026-10-23 pip-audit/Dependabot/Safety reportedly do not yet map this CVE to these PyPI packages, so scanner silence is not proof of being unaffected.
